title: task edit cannot unset a priority: --priority "" stores an empty string instead of clearing the field
description: Found 2026-10-28 while reverting QCLI-251 during the QCLI-538 grooming (record: QCLI-538 notes). QCLI-251 had no priority key. `quest task edit QCLI-251 --priority medium` set one, and `quest task edit QCLI-251 --priority ""` then stored `"priority":""` rather than removing the key; `task view` read it back as an empty string, not null. There is no clear-priority flag (compare --clear-milestone, --clear-parent). The only way back to the original record was `git checkout <ref> -- <file>`, which bypasses quest. An empty-string priority is also outside the configured vocabulary (low, medium, high, critical), so quest doctor would report task_vocabulary_off_set for it. Reproduce against `bun src/cli/main.ts` before fixing, per the installed-vs-dev rule.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A priority set on a task can be cleared through quest, so task view reads it as null and the stored record has no priority key
An empty-string --priority is either refused with a validation error naming the clear path or treated as that clear, and the choice is stated in the manifest and help
The new behavior has a test in both directions: a set-then-clear round trip, and the empty-string case
